briefdescription.para: Core orchestrator for the bsm4tops-gnn-analysis framework.

detaileddescription.para: The AnalysisG::analysis class is the central component responsible for managing and executing the various stages of a physics analysis, from data input and processing to model training and inference. It integrates functionalities from several other modules, including data loading (dataloader), sample tracing (sampletracer), I/O operations (io), event and graph building, selection application, metric evaluation, and model management.

This class provides a high-level interface for users to define their analysis pipeline by adding samples, event/graph templates, selections, metrics, and models. It handles the intricate details of data flow, caching, multi-threading, and interaction with external libraries like ROOT and potentially CUDA for accelerated computing.

The analysis class follows a structured approach to manage the analysis workflow:
Initialization: Sets up paths, initializes helper objects (tracer, loader, reader), and prepares the environment for PCM (Plugin-in C++ Modules) compilation if necessary. It dynamically compiles meta-data structs and other necessary components using gSystem and std::thread for parallel compilation.
Configuration: Users configure the analysis by adding various components:
add_samples: Specifies input ROOT files and their corresponding labels.
add_event_template: Defines how raw events are transformed into structured event objects.
add_graph_template: Specifies how event objects are converted into graph representations.
add_selection_template: Applies cuts and filters to events or graphs.
add_metric_template: Defines metrics for evaluating models or analysis performance.
add_model: Registers models for training or inference, optionally with optimizer parameters.
Execution (start() method):
Initializes settings, including debug mode and thread count.
Checks and manages data caching for graphs.
Orchestrates the building of events, selections, and graphs.
Compiles tracer objects for efficient data processing.
Builds the data loader, preparing data for training/inference.
Manages metric fold creation.
Handles graph caching (dumping and restoring).
Initiates model training sessions (if configured) by starting a CUDA server and building the project.
Initiates model inference sessions (if configured) by starting a CUDA server.

The class extensively uses std::map and std::vector for managing various configurations and data structures, ensuring flexibility and scalability. It also leverages ROOT's RDataFrame for efficient data processing and TSystem for file system interactions and dynamic code compilation.
